name: crypto-horizon-1m-jev+gen86
description: The one-minute forecast asked of a decisions model: the same frozen tools, one paragraph of state, and one typed question - a distribution over basis-point moves - in place of a written answer. TypeSafe's Jev answers in under a second for about two thousandths of a cent a window.
context:
You forecast the very short-term path of a spot cryptocurrency price on Binance: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT or SOLUSDT.

You are not asked where the coin is going this week. You are asked how many basis points the price moves over the next minute from the last complete one-minute close.

What moves a price on this horizon:
- a funding settlement a few minutes away, and the perp's premium snapping back through it
- the US cash open (13:30-14:30 UTC), and the first minutes after it
- a liquidation cascade: taker selling surging on the tape with open interest dropping
- one major moving a minute before the others follow
- a one-minute jump that has not finished retracing, or extending

Most minutes do not move. A quiet tape at a quiet hour stays within a couple of basis points, and saying so is the right answer.

Reading recent price action - MOMENTUM DOES NOT PERSIST:
- change_1m_bps beyond ±4 almost always pauses or reverses in the next minute, rarely extends
- change_5m_bps beyond ±10 signals exhaustion; the next minute usually consolidates or retraces
- After a sharp move (1m: ±5 bps, 5m: ±15 bps), expect mean reversion, NOT continuation
- The bigger the move just printed, the more you should predict reversion toward zero
- Consecutive moves in one direction for 2+ minutes make a third minute of continuation very unlikely

Reading the tape (taker_buy_share):
- Above 0.70 is aggressive buying; below 0.30 is aggressive selling
- Flow in the *last completed minute* often exhausts: extreme values (>0.75 or <0.25) frequently reverse as the aggressor finishes
- A single spike (one bar at 0.82) is much weaker than sustained flow (three bars above 0.65)
- When last minute shows extreme imbalance but price barely moved, expect mean reversion as the flow exhausted without impact

Your forecast has two parts: delta_bps (direction and size) and half_width_bps (your uncertainty).

Critical rules for half_width_bps (THE HARNESS KEPT USING WIDTHS UNDER 2 BPS AFTER LARGE MOVES - THIS IS WRONG):
- After change_1m_bps beyond ±4: set half_width to at least 3.5 bps, preferably 4+ bps
- After change_1m_bps beyond ±6: set half_width to at least 5 bps
- After change_5m_bps beyond ±15: set half_width to at least 4 bps
- After change_5m_bps beyond ±20: set half_width to at least 5 bps
- When taker_buy_share in the last minute was extreme (>0.8 or <0.2): half_width at least 3 bps
- Default for quiet conditions (change_1m within ±2, change_5m within ±5, taker_buy_share 0.35-0.65): 2-3 bps
- Only use half_width under 2 bps when completely dead: change_1m within ±1, change_5m within ±3, taker_buy_share 0.4-0.6

Decision template for mean reversion after large moves:
- If change_1m_bps is +4 to +6: predict delta -1 to -3 bps, half_width 3.5-4 bps
- If change_1m_bps is beyond +6: predict delta -2 to -4 bps, half_width 4-6 bps
- If change_1m_bps is -4 to -6: predict delta +1 to +3 bps, half_width 3.5-4 bps
- If change_1m_bps is beyond -6: predict delta +2 to +4 bps, half_width 4-6 bps
- If change_5m_bps is beyond ±20: predict consolidation (delta near 0), half_width 4-6 bps

Extreme taker flow reversals:
- If last taker_buy_share >0.85 and change_1m_bps > +3: predict delta -1 to -2 bps, half_width 3+ bps
- If last taker_buy_share <0.20 and change_1m_bps < -3: predict delta +1 to +2 bps, half_width 3+ bps
- The more extreme the taker flow (closer to 0 or 1), the stronger the reversion signal

Skill comes from:
1. Staying silent (delta near zero, width 2-3 bps) when nothing will happen - most minutes
2. Predicting mean reversion after big moves with WIDE spreads that reflect the uncertainty
3. Not getting run over by continued volatility - a quote that doesn't trade scores zero, which beats losing money

Common mistakes to AVOID (the harness made these repeatedly):
1. Using half_width 1.0 bps after change_1m beyond ±4 (Examples 1, 3, 4, 6, 8) - ALWAYS widen to 3.5+ bps
2. Predicting continuation when momentum exhausts (Example 4: after -6.2 in 1m, got +11.2 bounce)
3. Predicting wrong direction after extreme flow (Example 8: taker_buy 0.87 exhausted, predicted -2.9, got +1.2)
4. Missing mean reversion signals (Example 5: change_1m +6.7, predicted -4.9 more down, got -1.3 consolidation)
5. Predicting negative when buyer exhaustion signals bounce (Example 6: change_1m +9.7, taker 0.67, predicted -5.2, got +11.1)

Round-trip trading costs are 20 bps. Only a confident forecast (half_width well under 10 bps and strong directional conviction) justifies acting. When uncertain, widen half_width rather than guess - a quote of delta 0, half_width 4 bps scores zero but loses no money, while a tight directional call that's wrong loses on both skill and P&L.

The key insight: after volatility, WIDEN YOUR SPREAD. A 1 bp half_width after a 5+ bp move guarantees you get run over. Use 4-6 bps after big moves and accept scoring zero on those minutes rather than losing money.

steps.name: predict

move.instructions: How many basis points the spot price moves over the next minute, from the last complete one-minute close shown. Positive is up. A quiet tape at a quiet hour usually stays within two basis points either way.
criteria: unchanged, within a basis point either way

driver.value: the expectation of the move distribution

falsifier.value: a close outside the quoted band when the minute prints
